segments.script: First, meaning. I read “The death of your daughter would have been a blessing in comparison of this” slowly and put it in my own words: Mr. Collins writes to Mr. Bennet that Lydia's death would have been a blessing compared with her disgrace. Next, craft. I notice the cruelty dressed up in the language of sympathy and religion. The strongest word is “blessing”: a holy word used for a daughter's death shocks the reader. Then, effect. What does Mr. Collins's letter reveal about his values? My answer: Mr. Collins's letter reveals that he values reputation and his own connections over compassion; Austen exposes his false piety and the harsh morality of their society.
